silo_relevance: This paper is highly relevant to trading_execution because it targets fill-probability estimation for RFQ responses, a core execution and market-making decision problem. Its main contribution is a hybrid feature-generation approach that uses quantum hardware-transformed market-state inputs to improve out-of-sample execution prediction on real intraday corporate bond trading data.

key_points.point: Directly addresses fill-probability estimation for RFQ execution decisions in market making.
key_points.silo_note: Execution quality in trading_execution depends on predicting whether a quote will fill, so this is the paper's core domain fit.

key_points.point: Uses market-state representations built from RFQ and surrounding market information as the input to execution models.
key_points.silo_note: Trading_execution systems rely on rich pre-trade state features; this paper's feature construction is directly about modeling the state that drives execution likelihood.

key_points.point: Proposes an offline quantum feature-generation step that can be decoupled from the online response system.
key_points.silo_note: This matters for trading_execution because it preserves a practical real-time response workflow while using heavier feature transforms offline.

key_points.point: Reports up to 34% out-of-sample uplift when classical models consume hardware-transformed features.
key_points.silo_note: For execution and market-making, even modest predictive gains can affect quoting and response quality; the reported uplift suggests potential value in execution models.

key_points.point: The results are empirical and dataset-specific, with unresolved noise effects and no general causal claim.
key_points.silo_note: For trading_execution deployment, this limits how confidently one can generalize the reported gains to other instruments, venues, or execution regimes.
